next_step: POC scale test w/ 50M vectors; security sweep + connector spec
company_description: Mid-size enterprise analytics provider for wealth management firms. Heavily document-driven workflows (research notes, regulatory filings, client memos). Current search is Elastic on-prem + bespoke semantic pipeline; evaluating migration to a vector-first architecture.
notes: Summary: Evaluating Redwood for RAG stack to support large-scale internal search across research + compliance corpora.
Key pain: current Elastic + custom embeddings struggles at scale (50M+ chunks) — high cost, inconsistent latency, no solid reranking layer.
Scale targets: target index ~50M chunks (~10-12M docs), expect 200M embeddings after chunking/versions. Need plan for growth to 200M+ vectors in 18 months.
Latency/throughput targets: p95 end-to-end (ANN + rerank) <= 150ms for simple queries; sustained 50 qps, burst to 200 qps. Cost-per-query target <$0.003 (embeddings + ANN + single small rerank).

Current infra: Elastic on-prem for BM25; embeddings pipeline (in-house) using 768-d open model, stored in Postgres + pgvector for small datasets. Trying to avoid vendor lock but open to managed if meets SLAs.

Vector DB preferences being evaluated: Pinecone (managed), Weaviate (open + vectorized plug-ins), pgvector (self-hosted), Elastic Vector (integrated but expensive at scale). Need connector spec for each.

Connector requirements (explicit ask): streaming upserts, idempotent upserts, point-in-time snapshots, incremental reindexing w/ diff delta, bulk batch size tuning, backpressure handling, and guaranteed ordering for versioned docs.

Hybrid search needs: fall back to BM25 for low-signal queries; support routed policy (semantic-first for long queries, lexical-first for short/keyword queries). Token-level caching for frequent queries requested.

Reranking: prefer light-weight instruction-tuned re-ranker (<=2B params) deployed at edge or dedicated pool. Reranker must accept candidate scores + tokens and return calibrated scores; Redwood re-ranker integration points asked for.
Indexing concerns: cold-start index build time target <12 hours for 50M vectors; incremental adds should not degrade query latency. Shard/replica planning and warm-up strategy required.
Quantization & memory: interest in int8/4-bit quantized embeddings & model quantization to reduce infra cost. Need guidance from Redwood Optimize on tradeoffs for recall/regression risk.
Privacy/regulatory: PII redaction before embeddings, retention policies (7y and selective purge), strict egress controls — must support KMS + HSM, and audit log export to SIEM.
Networking / deployment: preference for VPC peering w/ customer-managed subnet. On-prem option considered for regulated customers (air-gapped acceptable with USB transfer option for model artifacts).

Security review status: initial questionnaire completed (drive link). SOC2 + ISO27001 demonstrated fine, but data residency & KMS flow require architecture diagram. SEC team wants certificate for HSM integration.
Cost modeling: finance gave ceiling ~ $0.003/query incl ANN + rerank. Current Elastic cost ~ $0.01/query at scale — large potential savings if Redwood Optimize can show 3x reduction.
Quote from CTO: "We need semantics at scale without the latency surprise; if we can get consistent p95 under 150ms and predictable TCO, we'll move quickly."

POC ask: Redwood to provide connector proof-of-concept for pgvector (self-hosted) + Pinecone (managed) showing: throughput at 50 qps, p95 <= 150ms, cost model, and A/B of reranker on top of ANN candidates.
Technical notes from SE call (Lina): prefer batch upserts of 10k vectors, use payload filtering to keep index small, support pre-filtering on metadata (account_id, doc_type) for tenant isolation.
Operational: want observability hooks — per-route token & latency breakdown, per-index cardinality, cache hit ratio, and automated anomaly detection for recall drop. Redwood Console demo resonated.
Compliance: retention controls must allow "selective redact + re-embed" flow; legal flagged deletion SLA of 72 hours once purge is requested.
Integration asks: example connector code (Go and Python), Terraform module for connector + VPC peering, recommended buffer sizes and backoff policy for bulk loads.
Stakeholders: CTO (Anne Ribeiro), Head of Data (Daniel Cho), Security Lead (Priya Nair), Procurement (Rajesh Kumar).
Decision criteria: 1) performance at scale, 2) predictable TCO, 3) connector robustness and incremental reindexing, 4) enterprise security/compliance, 5) ops/observability.

Competitor notes: Pinecone pitched managed simplicity; Weaviate appealing for schema + Graph integrations; Elastic team promises unified stack but cost is concern. Internal pgvector attractive for control but ops overhead is high.
Next steps (short): schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-03-08, provide connector spec doc + cost model, SE to produce indexing runbook and latency profile by 2026-03-04.

Open questions: can Redwood guarantee <150ms p95 with reranker included at 50 qps? What's the cold-start index build for 50M vectors on dedicated vs private? How does Redwood handle incremental deletes and GDPR requests at scale?
Notes style: fragmented; phone notes, internal action items; include jira INF keys for escalations (listed above).
